ai.description: This skink reaches 40 cm in length. It features a robust body with a pale, orange-spotted back and a distinctively bright orange tail. It is distinguished by smooth scales and a pointed snout.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Eumeces schneiderii* is best distinguished by the presence of a single, large, undivided subocular scale that touches the lip, a feature absent in similar Indian skinks.
ai.habitat: *Eumeces schneiderii* inhabits arid to semi-arid rocky landscapes, scrublands, and sandy deserts, typically ranging from lowlands up to 2,000 meters in elevation.
ai.behavior: The Schneider's skink is primarily diurnal, actively foraging for insects and small vertebrates during the warmest parts of the day to maintain its body temperature.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Eumeces schneiderii* is oviparous, laying a single clutch of 4–20 eggs annually. Breeding typically occurs in spring, with hatching taking place in summer.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Eumeces schneiderii* occurs in the arid regions of northwestern India, primarily across Rajasthan and parts of Punjab, typically at low to moderate elevations.
